newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton and Yeltsin to meet in modern, airy villa.
newsitem.headline: Clinton and Yeltsin to meet in modern, airy villa.

text.p: Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin will hold the main meeting of their two-day summit in Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari's residence, a modern seaside villa free of associations with past Cold War meetings or presidents.

Built in 1993, Mantyniemi (pronounced Mantuniemi) or "Pine Point" nestles on a small promontory jutting out into the Baltic among pine trees and wooden villas, in parkland just outside the city centre.

Modern, airy and south-facing, Mantyniemi's mainly white interior spurns heavy forms and hard right-angles: sculptured in stone, wood and glass, its high ceilings and picture windows suggest the house is flooded in daylight.
Its main reception room holds elegant green upholstered furniture among glass sculptures and fresh, light-wooden floors, resembling a modern art gallery.
It usually houses a grand piano as well as a series of abstract paintings called "The Same Blood in All of Us".

Commenting on Finland's granite landscape, its main designer, Reima Pietila, wrote: "The building is...created on Finland's Cambrian Rock, which that great designer the Ice Age has wrought into a splendid structure."

Those with access to the Internet can inspect pictures of the venue and read the latest on the agenda for the summit, which takes place on Thursday and Friday, from page www.vn.fi/vn/um/finfo/english/summit.html.
